raw_response:
I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it fits my wells, and after 30 years I trust it more than trying to expand chili too much. Chili can bring better cash, but it takes more labor and closer field management, and with some family members working off-farm I will not put too much area into it. So I will put 8.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.1 mu for chili as my cash crop. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability, because I want steady production more than risk. For wheat, I will fertilize moderately and irrigate a few times since I have well water and want secure grain yield. For maize, I will keep fertilizer a little stronger on nitrogen and use fewer irrigations than wheat, because summer rain can help but I still want the well as backup. For chili, I will manage it more intensively, with more potassium, more irrigations, and more pesticide sprays, because chili is more sensitive and I am growing it for income, so I need better fruit set and cleaner pods. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it saves labor and suits my scale better than deep ploughing every time.
